title: Deploy a Private LLM for Business Without Data Leaks
summary: A private LLM for business provides a secure framework for evaluating infrastructure requirements and total ownership expenses.
body_markdown:
## Private LLM deployment models for regulated industries


Private LLM deployment occurs whenever you run models on infrastructure where you control the network perimeter. In this environment, data never leaves your verified environment to train a vendor’s base weights.


Moving beyond simple API calls, this setup requires a structured architecture where your chosen model, such as Claude Fable 5.1 for complex reasoning, resides within your own security boundary. The three primary deployment modes are:


- VPC-hosted (isolated cloud instance)
- On-premise (local server rack)
- Air-gapped (no external internet connection)


### Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) isolation


By renting high-performance hardware while maintaining a private network tunnel, businesses can use VPC isolation to prevent public internet exposure. For teams that need to scale[Gemini](https://gemini.google/subscriptions) 3.1 Pro for agentic coding without building a physical data center, this is the standard entry point.


The convenience of the cloud, however, carries a premium for the specialized H100 GPUs required to run frontier models.


[Intuition Labs](https://intuitionlabs.ai/articles/h100-rental-prices-cloud-comparison) reports that the hourly rental cost for an H100 is $6.98 on GCP and Azure, which means companies must budget **nearly seven dollars for every hour** of compute time.


AWS and Oracle charge $6.88 per hour, so choosing these providers offers a marginal cost advantage over their primary competitors.


Before you account for storage, a sustained reasoning cluster can cost over $5,000 monthly per card, making the long-term financial commitment for AI infrastructure substantial, which means companies must carefully weigh these recurring overheads against their projected project returns.


Specialized providers like Lambda Labs offer a lower rate of $3.99 per hour, allowing developers to significantly reduce their operational expenses compared to major cloud platforms, so teams can allocate more of their budget toward model development rather than raw compute costs.


If they don't require the broader ecosystem of a major hyper-scaler, teams can **reduce their infrastructure spend by nearly 43%** , freeing up capital for other development priorities.


### Running private LLMs on-premise server racks


To eliminate recurring rental fees and third-party data residency risks, companies can deploy on-premise by running models like Mistral Large 4 on physical server racks they own. Management of this mode is often handled via an[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) installation on a local Docker or Kubernetes cluster.


Reselling you a model is deciding your AI strategy for you, often at a significant markup. Activepieces runs whichever model you have already deployed (using your own provider keys and infrastructure) so that model spend lands on your own provider account at your own rate.


> Reselling you a model is deciding your AI strategy for you, often at a significant markup.


You can verify this Bring-Your-Own-Key availability by tier on the pricing page, ensuring the strategy remains yours to set rather than a vendor's to sell back to you.


### Air-gapped deployments for maximum data security


The highest level of security is provided by air-gapped environments, which **physically disconnect the model** and its data from the outside world. In air-gapped environments, this is the only way to guarantee that a compromised network gateway can't exfiltrate sensitive IP used with GPT-6 Astra.


Sovereign clouds follow a similar logic but are managed by local entities to comply with specific national data laws. Data remains under domestic jurisdiction even if a vendor is subpoenaed.
